(returns early). Therefore, when the `deleteCharAt` call is executed, `buffer.length()` is guaranteed to be at least 1, so the index `buffer.length() - 1` is valid (0 to length-1). The only declared exception for `deleteCharAt` (based on the javadoc) is `StringIndexOutOfBoundsException`, which is thrown when the index is negative or greater than or equal to the buffer's length. Since the index is always within bounds, this exception is fully avoided.
